proposal.description: The latch test compares the post-increment strike count against MAX_STRIKES-1, so the -1 for the pre-increment value is applied twice
proposal.reason: At the default max_strikes of 3, latch_assert rises on the second hiccup entry, when strike_level goes from 1 to 2, instead of the third. With max_strikes 2 it trips on the first hiccup.

proposal.description: The switching-cycle boundary is taken on both PWM edges, so each switching cycle counts twice toward the clean run
proposal.reason: In S_RUN, clean_counter reaches clean_run_target after half the intended number of switching cycles, so strike_level is cleared after about 0.5 s of fault-free running instead of 1 s.

proposal.description: The strike clear still waits for the old all-ones terminal count instead of clean_run_target, although the counter now saturates at the target
proposal.reason: At the default target, which is below all-ones, clean_counter stops at the target and never reaches all-ones. A strike earned by a hiccup is then never cleared, however long the run, and later isolated hiccups add up to latch_assert.

proposal.description: The clean-run counter saturates at all-ones, the old fixed terminal, instead of holding at clean_run_target
proposal.reason: If the host lowers clean_run_target to a value below the current clean count while strikes are outstanding, the original counter wraps around and then clears strike_level when it reaches the new target. The mutant holds at all-ones and never matches, so strike_level stays non-zero until the next hiccup.

proposal.description: The strike clear waits for the next switching-cycle boundary after the clean run completes, instead of happening on the next clock
proposal.reason: In S_RUN with strikes outstanding, strike_level goes to zero one full PWM period after clean_counter reaches clean_run_target, not on the next clk. If S_RUN is left within that period, the clear never happens.

proposal.description: A completed clean run forgives one strike instead of clearing the whole count, and keeps doing so while the clean count stays saturated
proposal.reason: After a clean run in S_RUN with strike_level at 1, the clear branch fires every clock while the counter holds at the target. strike_level steps 0, 3, 2, 1 and so on, so the next hiccup gets the wrong cool-down and can trip latch_assert on its first entry.
